newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE oil company to drill two wells in 1997 - MEES.
newsitem.headline: UAE oil company to drill two wells in 1997 - MEES.

text.p: The oil and gas company in the UAE emirate of Ras al-Khaimah will drill two exploration wells in the first quarter of 1997, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

The Cyprus-based weekly quoted Felix Malloy, general-manager of the Ras al-Khaimah Oil and Gas Co Ltd, as saying a decision on the drill site would be taken after onshore and offshore analysis of seismic data were completed by end-1996.
Top-ranking U.S. investor Michael Dingman signed an offshore and onshore oil and gas exploration deal with the emirate's ruler Sheikh Saqr bin Mohammed al-Qassimi in January.
The agreement has a 30-year term if production comes on stream within five years from the date of signature.
Ras al-Khaimah, located on the northeastern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, lacks the substantial hydrocarbon reserves of the United Arab Emirates' largest and wealthiest member, Abu Dhabi.
The small emirate's reserves are estimated at 400 million barrels of oil and condensate and 1,200 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
Ras al-Khaimah government has awarded nearly all of its onshore and offshore concession to the firm, except B-bloc offshore field held by the U.S. Atlantic Richfield Co.
Canada's International Petroleum Corp relinquished its exploration licence for the emirate's onshore field at the end of 1993 after a second well-drilling proved fruitless.
